newsitem.title: SPAIN: Clinton, Chirac urge Ukraine to reform for IMF aid.
newsitem.headline: Clinton, Chirac urge Ukraine to reform for IMF aid.

text.p: U.S. President Bill Clinton and French President Jacques Chirac both told Ukraine on Wednesday to press ahead with economic reforms this year if it wanted more international financial aid.
President Leonid Kuchma, meeting Chirac and Clinton separately on the margins of a NATO summit in Madrid, appealed for support for Ukraine's drive for International Monetary Fund (IMF) loans.
The IMF said recently it might delay a three-year $2.5-$3 billion loan meant for countries undertaking structural reforms and issue a limited stand-by loan in the meantime.

"I told President Kuchma that if he could find a way to support reforms and enact them in this year, I would do everything I could to see that the World Bank, the IMF and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) supported Ukraine," Clinton told a news conference.
He praised Ukraine's recent signing of an agreement with Russia settling outstanding differences, which he said had been Washington's biggest concern for security in the Black Sea area.
A French official said Chirac too praised the Ukraine-Russia agreement but listed a series of steps Ukraine needed to take to win further Western financial backing.

He cited a need to accelerate the privatisation of state enterprises, creeping along at snail's pace, pursue structural reforms and establish laws on transparency of the financial system and stability.
The French leader also recalled a pledge by Ukraine -- site of the Chernobyl nuclear disaster in 1986 -- to bring its former Soviet nuclear power plants up to Western safety standards.
He deplored the fact that some Western countries had not yet met their commitments under a Group of Seven agreement to finance the programme.

Clinton, who discussed the issue with Chirac in a private meeting on Tuesday, said he had renewed the G7's pledge, made in Denver last month, to help "Ukraine deal with the closure of Chernobyl and develop reasonable alternative sources of energy".
